body_markdown:
Artificial intelligence is advancing at remarkable speed, but Bill Gates believes the technology also requires stronger international safeguards. The Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist is reportedly seeking a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping later this year to discuss ways countries can work together to manage some of the most serious risks associated with advanced AI.


According to a report, Gates wants governments to pay particular attention to the possibility that increasingly capable AI systems could be used to design molecules or assist with biological attacks. He argues that international monitoring could help reduce these risks without preventing the wider technology industry from continuing to develop.


## Bill Gates Wants International Cooperation on AI Safety


Gates is expected to propose international initiatives aimed at addressing the risks created by rapidly developing AI systems. A spokesperson for Gates reportedly confirmed that his team is working to finalize a meeting with Xi during a planned visit to China, tentatively scheduled for November.


The potential meeting comes as governments around the world continue to debate how artificial intelligence should be regulated. AI has moved quickly from a specialized technology into a mainstream tool used across business, education, research, software development and many other areas.


However, the same capabilities that make advanced AI valuable can potentially create new security challenges. Gates has therefore emphasized the importance of governments cooperating before potentially dangerous applications become easier to access.


His position appears to be based on the idea that AI safety cannot be addressed effectively by one country acting alone. Because AI models and the research behind them operate across international borders, rules developed in one region may have limited impact if other countries take completely different approaches.


## Why Biological Risks Are Receiving Attention


One of Gates' major concerns is the possibility that AI could eventually make it easier to synthesize molecules or support activities connected to biological attacks.


AI can process enormous amounts of scientific information and assist researchers with complex problems. These capabilities can have legitimate benefits, including accelerating scientific research and potentially contributing to advances in medicine and biotechnology.


At the same time, powerful technologies can sometimes be misused. Gates wants countries to monitor whether AI systems are becoming capable of providing assistance that could create serious biological security risks.


Importantly, monitoring does not necessarily mean stopping scientific research or restricting every application of AI. Gates has argued that appropriate safeguards could be designed without preventing the technology sector from growing.


This distinction is central to the wider AI regulation debate. Governments face the difficult task of encouraging innovation while establishing protections against potentially dangerous uses of increasingly capable systems.


## Gates Believes China Could Play an Important Role


Gates also believes China could be an important participant in international discussions about AI safety.


According to the report, he believes China would potentially support restrictions on releasing hazardous AI models if the United States takes the initiative first. His comments suggest that cooperation between major AI powers could be important when dealing with risks that do not stop at national borders.


China has become a major player in artificial intelligence, while the United States remains home to many leading AI companies and research organizations. Decisions made by both countries could therefore influence the direction of AI development globally.


Gates' proposed discussions with Xi reflect the broader recognition that AI governance is becoming an international issue rather than simply a domestic policy question.


## The Importance of Responsible AI Development


The debate over AI safety is not only about regulation. It is also about how developers, researchers and governments define responsible technological progress.


Advanced AI systems are increasingly capable of performing sophisticated tasks. As those capabilities expand, policymakers are considering whether existing oversight mechanisms are sufficient.


The challenge is particularly complicated because technology develops faster than many traditional regulatory processes. Rules created today may need to account for capabilities that are still emerging.


Gates' focus on biological security highlights one specific area where this challenge could become significant. If AI systems eventually become more capable of assisting with advanced scientific or biological tasks, governments may need better ways to identify dangerous applications while preserving beneficial research.


This could involve international standards, monitoring systems, restrictions on particularly hazardous capabilities and greater communication between governments and technology companies.


## A Potential Turning Point for Global AI Policy


A meeting between Gates and Xi would not, by itself, create international AI regulations. However, direct discussions between influential figures from different countries could contribute to a broader conversation about shared responsibilities.


The technology industry has become increasingly global, meaning that AI safety measures may be more effective when major countries coordinate their approaches.


Gates' comments also demonstrate how the AI conversation is changing. Early discussions often focused on productivity, automation and economic growth. Those topics remain important, but attention is increasingly moving toward questions of security, misuse and the long-term consequences of powerful AI systems.


The biological threat discussed by Gates is particularly sensitive because it combines AI capabilities with existing concerns surrounding biological security. Any policies in this area would need to balance scientific openness and innovation against the possibility of malicious use.


## What Could Happen Next?


The next significant development may be whether Gates' proposed meeting with Xi is finalized. If the meeting takes place, AI governance and international cooperation could become important topics of discussion.


The wider issue, however, extends far beyond one meeting. Governments will continue to face decisions about how to regulate advanced AI, what types of capabilities require additional oversight and how countries can cooperate on risks that affect everyone.


For the technology sector, the challenge will be maintaining innovation while building effective safeguards. For governments, the task will be creating policies that are practical, internationally coordinated and flexible enough to keep pace with technological change.


Gates' warning is therefore part of a much larger global discussion. Artificial intelligence has the potential to deliver enormous benefits, but increasingly powerful systems may also introduce risks that require careful management.


As AI becomes more capable, international cooperation could become just as important as technological innovation itself.

*The Independent,* 26 August 2026.
